ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cluster-conditioned routing loss in a 1.3B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 1.3B parameters on 60B tokens of English and Chinese web text, books and mathematical text, using 2 seeds. Group token embeddings from a warm-started dense model into 32 clusters, and add a loss rewarding agreement between a token's cluster and its selected experts, weighted 0.02 beside the load-balancing term. Evaluate validation perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and RACE, and log cluster histograms of each expert at checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same network under load balancing only. Control: the same loss with shuffled cluster assignments. Ablation: loss weight 0.005 versus 0.1 on the smallest checkpoint. Overlap is measured by a pairwise Jaccard index on routed token sets.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Perplexity should improve slightly and the downstream average gain about one point, with expert overlap falling by a third. The idea fails if clusters mostly encode token frequency, steering experts toward frequency bands rather than functions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cosine penalty between expert outputs in a 6B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 24-expert, top-3 mixture-of-experts transformer with 6B parameters on 180B tokens of English text, Chinese text and mathematics, using 2 seeds. Penalize the dot product between mean output vectors of experts that process the same sequence, weighted 0.015 with the global-batch load-balancing loss, so experts that share a context are pushed toward different functions. Evaluate held-out loss in both languages, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval and DROP, plus the effective rank of stacked expert outputs at 6 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the same model with global-batch balancing only. Control: the penalty applied to randomly paired experts. Ablation: penalty weight 0.004 versus 0.04 on the first 20B tokens. Separation is read from the Jaccard index on routed token sets and the effective rank of outputs.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Effective rank should grow and held-out loss improve by about 0.01 nats, with a downstream gain near one point. The idea fails if cosine separation arises from norm differences alone, which would be of little use for specialization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Overlap penalty on routed token sets in a 300M mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Train an 8-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 300M active parameters on 15B tokens of English and Chinese text and math problems, using 3 seeds. After each micro-batch, form a soft overlap score between the token sets of each expert pair, and minimize it with weight 0.05 beside load balancing. Report perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and CMRC, plus the overlap score on held-out text at 4 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with identical data order. Control: the same term on tokens permuted within the batch, which keeps its magnitude but erases structure. Ablation: weights 0.01 and 0.2 at the first 5B tokens. A shared-expert variant is the reference for the architectural route.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Overlap should fall by about 40% and perplexity improve by a small amount, with benchmark results moving by well under a point. The effect could vanish if lower overlap is reached by assigning tokens at random.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Determinantal diversity term on expert embeddings in a 500M mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 500M active parameters on 20B tokens of English and Chinese web text and mathematical problems, using 5 seeds. Take the mean routed token embedding of each expert and add a log-determinant diversity term on their similarity matrix, weighted 0.012 with load balancing. Report perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and RACE, plus the log-determinant at 6 checkpoints, for weights 0.004 and 0.012.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with identical data order. Control: the same term on a similarity matrix of randomly chosen tokens. Ablation: a router-weight orthogonality term and a weight 0.1 as comparators. A paired bootstrap on held-out sequences gives intervals for each gap.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The log-determinant should rise steadily and perplexity improve by a small amount. The term could fail by driving mean embeddings apart through a few outlier tokens, leaving behavior unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Annealed domain supervision of routers in a 12B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 64-expert, top-6 fine-grained mixture-of-experts network of 12B parameters on 400B tokens spanning English text, Chinese text, mathematics and exam material, using 1 seed. During the first 15 percent of training, supervise the router with domain tags through a cross-entropy term mapping each domain to a subset of experts, then anneal it to zero while load balancing continues. Measure language-modeling loss, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval, CMMLU and CMRC.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with the same schedule. Control: the tag term with domain tags shuffled across documents, and a tag term kept at full weight throughout. Ablation: the supervised share at 5% and 30%, and expert-to-domain correlation measured after the term is removed.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Routing should keep a domain structure after supervision ends, with downstream gains of one to two points. It fails if the structure fades once the term is removed, which would show that specialization needs a persistent signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frequency-bucket routing loss in a 2B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 2B parameters on 300B tokens of English and Chinese text, using 2 seeds. Bucket tokens by corpus frequency into 8 groups and maximize mutual information between expert choice and bucket, conditioned on token position, weighted 0.03 beside load balancing. Evaluate perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval, CMRC and a long-context retrieval set, and keep checkpoints for the specialization curves.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with matched data order. Control: bucket labels from a hash of the token id, which encode nothing about frequency. Ablation: removing the position conditioning, and a lower and a higher loss weight. Expert-bucket mutual information is scored on held-out text.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Mutual information should rise clearly and perplexity improve slightly, with downstream movement of one point at most. The loss could fail by sorting experts into frequency bands that add no skill.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-wise balancing in a 3B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 3B parameters on 120B tokens, building each batch from a single source among English web, Chinese web, mathematics and reading material, using 2 seeds. Replace the global load-balancing loss with one inside each domain, and add a term separating the domain-level expert distributions, weighted 0.02. Evaluate language-modeling loss on held-out English and Chinese corpora, then GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval and CMRC, with usage profiles logged by domain.
CONTROLS: Baseline: mixed batches with global load balancing. Control: single-domain batches with the standard global loss, which separates the effect of batching from the effect of the objective. Ablation: weights 0.005 and 0.05. Domain distinctness is measured by the Jensen-Shannon distance between expert usage profiles.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: Usage profiles should diverge between domains and benchmark averages rise by around one point. A failure would show as unstable training from single-domain batches, which could erase any gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Kernel dependence penalty in a 1B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 1B parameters on 40B tokens of English and Chinese web text, textbooks and mathematics, using 3 seeds. Estimate a kernel dependence measure between outputs of different experts on the same tokens, and minimize it with weight 0.02 beside load balancing, restricted in separate runs to each of 12 layers or to all layers. Report validation perplexity for both languages, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and CMRC.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone. Control: a penalty on dependence with the output at a randomly drawn, different token. Ablation: kernel bandwidth at 3 settings and weights 0.005 and 0.08 for the all-layer run. A cosine-similarity penalty is the nearest simpler alternative.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: Dependence should fall by about half and the downstream average rise by at most one point, with most of the gain from a few layers. Failure is possible if lower dependence arises from noise added to expert outputs, which would hurt perplexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frequency-bucket routing loss in a 100M mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Train an 8-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 100M active parameters on 8B tokens of English and Chinese text, using 3 seeds. Bucket tokens by corpus frequency into 8 groups and add a loss maximizing mutual information between expert choice and bucket, conditioned on token position, weighted 0.03 beside load balancing. Evaluate perplexity in both languages and zero-shot accuracy on a small reading-comprehension set and a math word-problem set.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with matched data order. Control: bucket labels from a hash of the token id, which carry no frequency information. Ablation: removing the position conditioning. Specialization is scored by expert-bucket agreement on held-out text.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Mutual information should rise clearly and perplexity improve slightly, while the small downstream sets will be too noisy to read. The loss could fail by sorting experts into frequency bands that add no skill.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sequence-level routing entropy objective in a 1.5B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 32-expert, top-4 mixture-of-experts transformer with 1.5B active parameters on 90B tokens of English and Chinese text, using 3 seeds. Add a term lowering the entropy of each token's routing distribution at sequence level while global-batch balancing keeps usage even, weighted 0.01 and ramped over early training. Evaluate perplexity in both languages and accuracy on GSM8K, MMLU and C-Eval.
CONTROLS: Baseline: global-batch load balancing alone. Control: a temperature change of the router softmax that reaches the same entropy without any loss term. Ablation: ramp length at two values. Specialization is read from usage entropy at sequence and batch levels on held-out text.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Sequence-level entropy should fall while batch-level entropy stays high, with downstream gains under one point. The objective could fail if sharper routing makes training less stable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert-pair overlap penalty in a 7B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 64-expert, top-8 mixture-of-experts language model of 7B total parameters on 250B tokens of English text, Chinese text, mathematics and exam-style material, using 2 seeds. Add a soft overlap penalty between token sets of expert pairs within each sequence, weighted 0.02 beside global-batch load balancing. Evaluate loss, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval and CMRC.
CONTROLS: Baseline: global-batch balancing alone. Control: the same penalty on randomly paired experts. Ablation: weights 0.005 and 0.08 on the first 30B tokens, and a router-weight orthogonality term as the closest rival. Overlap is tracked by a Jaccard index at 6 checkpoints.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The overlap index should fall by a third and downstream scores rise by one to two points. The penalty could fail if lower overlap is achieved through near-random assignment of tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Topic-label contrastive routing loss in a 5B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 32-expert, top-4 mixture-of-experts transformer with 5B parameters on 150B tokens of English and Chinese text, using 2 seeds. Assign each sequence a topic from a 50-topic model fitted offline, and add a contrastive loss pulling the mean routing vectors of same-topic sequences together and pushing different-topic ones apart, weighted 0.03 beside load balancing. Evaluate loss each 5B tokens on 8 held-out corpora, then GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval, CMMLU, DROP, CMRC and RACE.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone. Control: random topic assignments with the same topic frequencies. Ablation: the topic count at 20 and 100, and token-level in place of sequence-level routing vectors in the contrastive loss.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Same-topic sequences should share experts more often, with downstream gains near one point. The loss fails if the topics line up with language identity alone, giving a two-cluster split instead of fine specialization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router supervision from pseudo-domains in a 2B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Train a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 2B parameters on 80B tokens of English and Chinese web text, textbooks and mathematics, using 2 seeds. Cluster documents into 12 pseudo-domains with a frozen sentence encoder, and supervise the router with them through a cross-entropy term, weighted 0.02 beside load balancing and dropped after 20B tokens. Report perplexity for both languages, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and CMRC.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone. Control: the cross-entropy term with pseudo-domain labels shuffled across documents. Ablation: encoder choice at 2 settings and the drop point at 10B and 40B tokens. Separation is read from expert-domain mutual information after the drop.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Mutual information should stay high after the term is dropped and the downstream average rise by one point or less. The loss may fail if the clusters follow document length rather than subject.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Warm-up routing diversity loss in a 1B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Train a 16-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 1B parameters on 400B tokens of English and Chinese web text, books and mathematics, using 2 seeds. Add a diversity loss on the pairwise cosine similarity of router weight vectors during the first 8 percent of training only, weighted 0.05 beside load balancing, so the effect on early expert separation can be read. Report perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, MMLU, C-Eval and CMRC.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone. Control: the same loss applied for the whole run. Ablation: a shorter and a longer warm-up fraction, and weights 0.01 and 0.2. Separation is scored by the pairwise Jaccard index of routed token sets at 5 checkpoints.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Early separation should be visible within the first 5B tokens and persist, with downstream gains under one point. Failure may come from the experts drifting back toward overlap once the loss stops.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router-sharpness objective in a 20B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 64-expert, top-8 mixture-of-experts language model of 20B total parameters on 1T tokens of English text, Chinese text, mathematics and exam-style material, using 1 seed. Add a term lowering the entropy of each token's routing distribution at sequence level while global-batch load balancing keeps total usage even, weighted 0.01 and ramped over the first 10 percent of training. Evaluate loss, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval, CMMLU, DROP and RACE.
CONTROLS: Baseline: global-batch balancing alone. Control: a temperature change of the router softmax that reaches the same entropy without any loss term. Ablation: ramp length at 2 values, and usage entropy at sequence and batch levels as the specialization measure.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Sequence-level entropy should fall while batch-level entropy stays high, with downstream gains of one to two points. The objective could fail if sharper routing makes training less stable at this size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pairwise expert dissimilarity regularizer in a 4B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 48-expert, top-6 mixture-of-experts transformer with 4B parameters on 150B tokens of English text, Chinese text, mathematics and reading material, using 2 seeds. Regularize the dissimilarity of expert feed-forward weights through a penalty on their pairwise dot product, weighted 0.04 with global-batch load balancing. Evaluate language-modeling loss, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval and RACE, and measure routing entropy at checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline: global-batch balancing alone. Control: the penalty applied to a random rotation of the weights, which keeps magnitude but loses their identity. Ablation: weights 0.002 and 0.02 early in training, and router orthogonality as the closest rival.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Pairwise alignment should fall and held-out loss improve by about 0.01 nats, with downstream gains of a point or less. It could fail if dissimilar weights do not translate into distinct routing, leaving behavior unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-conditioned expert dropout in a 700M mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Train an 8-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 700M active parameters on 30B tokens of English and Chinese text and mathematical problems, using 2 seeds. For each domain, disable a random quarter of experts during training so the remaining ones must cover its tokens, with a rotation each 500 steps, beside load balancing. Report perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and CMRC, and routing histograms per domain.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with identical data order. Control: random expert dropout not tied to domain. Ablation: disabled fractions of 12% and 50%, and rotation each 100 steps. Separation is scored by expert-domain mutual information on held-out text.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Mutual information should rise and perplexity stay within a small tolerance of the baseline. The approach could fail if dropout merely lowers quality for all domains alike.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-diversity routing loss in a 400M mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Train an 8-expert, top-2 mixture-of-experts transformer with 400M active parameters on 25B tokens of English and Chinese text and mathematical problems, using 5 seeds. Add a loss that lowers the alignment between gradients of different experts on the same batch, weighted 0.025 with load balancing, with 3 weights, 2 data orders and 4 routing temperatures. Report perplexity in both languages, GSM8K, C-Eval and RACE, and gradient similarity at 6 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline: load balancing alone with identical data order. Control: the same loss on gradients taken from different batches. Ablation: a router-weight orthogonality term and gradient alignment with sign removed. Paired bootstrap intervals on held-out sequences give each gap.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Gradient alignment should fall steadily and perplexity improve slightly, with downstream movement of well under a point. The term could fail if gradient noise dominates the signal at this batch size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Topic-aware load balancing in a 3B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 32-expert, top-4 mixture-of-experts transformer with 3B parameters on 100B tokens of English and Chinese text, using 2 seeds. Replace the global balancing target with one that asks each topic's sequences to use experts evenly inside a topic-specific subset of 8 experts, with topics from a 40-topic model fitted offline, and weight 0.02. Evaluate loss, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval and RACE.
CONTROLS: Baseline: global balancing alone. Control: random topic assignments with the same frequencies. Ablation: subset sizes of 4 and 16 experts, and a shared-expert variant as the architectural reference. Specialization is read from topic-expert correlation on held-out text.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Topic-expert correlation should rise and downstream scores gain around one point. The scheme fails if topics collapse into language identity, giving a two-way split.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert-choice entropy regularizer in an 8B mixture of experts
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 64-expert, top-8 mixture-of-experts transformer with 8B total parameters on 300B tokens of English text, Chinese text, mathematics and exam-style material, using 2 seeds. Regularize the entropy of the distribution of tokens each expert accepts, so that each expert concentrates on a narrow slice of the data, with weight 0.015 beside global-batch load balancing. Evaluate loss, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, C-Eval, CMMLU, DROP and RACE.
CONTROLS: Baseline: global-batch balancing alone. Control: a regularizer on a random subset of tokens of equal size. Ablation: weights 0.006 and 0.06 during the first 40B tokens. Concentration is read from the entropy of per-expert token-frequency profiles at 8 checkpoints.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Per-expert entropy should fall and downstream gains reach one to two points. It could fail if concentration is achieved by experts splitting along frequency lines, which adds no skill.
